When I began sharing my thoughts on HumbleDollar, I never imagined how much I would receive in return. Readers I’ve never met have offered encouragement, shared their own experiences, and reminded me that the written word can connect people who may never meet. For that, I am deeply grateful.
p

But beyond HumbleDollar, my gratitude extends to those who have stepped forward to help me and my family over the past year. I’ve come to realize that gratitude becomes more meaningful when we understand how quickly life can change.
p

Sometimes it’s the person who remembers what you’ve been through, the friend who calls just to see how you’re doing, or someone who offers help without being asked. There are so many people to thank. You know who you are, and you will forever have a place in my heart.
p
Then there are those I’ve met along the way, people whose kindness and integrity have inspired me to write about experiences that might otherwise have gone untold.
p

There’s Alissa, Doug, Karina, Nico and Brondan at Boca Auto Fix, who reminded me that honesty and trust still matter in business. And Steve W., Steve S., and Bill, whose confidence in my brother and me helped our business thrive and ultimately allowed us to retire early. Their stories became part of my writing, but their contributions to my life began long before I put pen to paper.
p

And then there’s Joey, who has helped carry me through one of the most difficult years of our lives. His patience, understanding, and unwavering support have kept me grounded as we navigate life’s challenges together. Through the difficult moments and the joyful ones, his love and kindness have been a constant source of strength. For that, I am forever grateful.
p

Growing older is something we often complain about. Yet I’ve come to see each additional year as something worth celebrating. Not everyone is given the privilege of growing old, and after losing two siblings, that’s something I try never to forget.
p

I’m also thankful for the financial security that allows me to enjoy this stage of life. Not necessarily for what money can buy, but for the freedom it provides: time with Joey, opportunities to travel, the ability to help my mother, and the freedom to write.
p
Having enough is a wonderful thing. But perhaps recognizing that we have enough is an even greater gift.
p

And so, as Thanksgiving approaches, I find myself returning to where this reflection began: the HumbleDollar community. To those who have taken the time to read my articles, share their stories, or leave a few encouraging words, thank you. You’ve given me far more than you may realize.
p

Jonathan created something special here, a place where conversations about money so often become conversations about life. I’m grateful that his words brought us together and that, through all of you, something of him continues to live on.
p
What better reason could there be to give thanks?
